theme: The resurrection; Thomas; the reinstatement of Peter
readingInstruction: Read John 20:1-21:25. The empty tomb, the appearance to Mary Magdalene, to the disciples, and to Thomas, the purpose statement of the Gospel, and a breakfast on the beach where Jesus restores Peter. Read 20:30-31 slowly.
settingTheScene: It is early on the first day of the week, while it is still dark. Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb and finds the stone taken away. John’s account is intimate and personal. He tells of his own race with Peter to the tomb, of Mary’s tears, of Thomas’s doubt, and of a morning by the Sea of Tiberias. The Gospel was originally written to end at chapter 20; chapter 21 is an epilogue that answers Peter’s denial.
observation: “Jesus said to her, Mary. She turned and said to him in Aramaic, Rabboni!” (20:16).
“As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you” (20:21).
“Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed” (20:29).
“But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name” (20:31).
“Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?” (21:15).
“Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you” (21:17).
interpretation:
Mary finds the tomb empty and runs to tell Peter and John. They run to the tomb. John arrives first but Peter goes in first, and they see the linen cloths lying there. John “saw and believed.” Mary stays outside, weeping. Two angels ask why she is weeping, and then she turns and sees Jesus, but does not recognize him, thinking he is the gardener. He says one word: “Mary.” She knows his voice. “Rabboni!” The good shepherd calls his sheep by name. He sends her to the disciples: “I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.”

That evening, the disciples are behind locked doors. Jesus stands among them: “Peace be with you.” He shows them his hands and side. “As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you.” He breathes on them and says, “Receive the Holy Spirit.” He gives them authority to proclaim the forgiveness of sins.

Thomas was not there. He says he will not believe unless he sees the nail marks and puts his hand in his side. A week later, Jesus appears again. “Put your finger here, and see my hands.” Thomas does not need to touch. He says the greatest confession in the Gospel: “My Lord and my God!” Jesus says, “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” That includes every Christian since.

Then John states his purpose. Jesus did many other signs, but these are written “so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.” John selected his signs to produce faith. Everything in this Gospel is to bring us to belief, and life.

Chapter 21 shows Peter, who denied Jesus three times by a charcoal fire, restored by another charcoal fire. Seven disciples have gone fishing and caught nothing. A man on the shore tells them to cast on the right side, and the net is full. “It is the Lord!” Peter jumps in. On the beach Jesus has breakfast ready. Then he asks Peter three times, “Do you love me?” Peter is grieved, and says, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Each time Jesus gives him a charge: “Feed my lambs… Tend my sheep… Feed my sheep.” The one who denied him is made a shepherd. Jesus also tells him how he will die and ends with “Follow me.” The Gospel ends with John’s note that the world could not contain the books if everything Jesus did were written.
connection: Genesis 2 and 3 take place in a garden, as does the resurrection in John. Psalm 16:10 and Isaiah 53:10-12 speak of the Messiah’s rising. Genesis 2:7 describes the breath of life, echoed in 20:22. Ezekiel 37:9-14 speaks of breath and the Spirit giving life. Luke 24:36-49 gives the parallel appearance. 1 Corinthians 15:3-8 lists the witnesses to the resurrection. 1 Peter 1:8 says that though you have not seen him, you love him. 1 Peter 5:1-4 is Peter’s later call to shepherd the flock.
application:
Hear Jesus call your name as he called Mary’s. Respond with “Rabboni.”

Confess with Thomas, “My Lord and my God,” and mean it.

If you have failed Jesus, hear him ask, “Do you love me?” and answer honestly.
prayerPrompts: Say to Jesus, “My Lord and my God,” and mean it.
Thank him for calling you by name.
Hear him ask, “Do you love me?” and answer him.
